result.title: Counterfactual Rollouts for Offline Contrastive Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Contrastive reinforcement learning (CRL) learns goal-conditioned values by associating state--action pairs with the states subsequently reached, assuming that no unobserved variable jointly affects the recorded action and its outcome. When offline demonstrations come from a demonstrator with information hidden from the learner, this assumption fails and the critic absorbs spurious action--outcome associations. We formalize this setting with confounded Markov decision processes and introduce counterfactual transitions that separate what the data identify from what they do not; minimizing over all compatible transitions yields a worst-case occupancy that lower-bounds the true one. Causal Contrastive Reinforcement Learning (CauCRL) learns a pessimistic counterfactual transition from positive and negative offline demonstrations and trains the critic on counterfactual rollouts, substantially improving success rates over standard CRL on confounded goal-reaching tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究离线目标条件强化学习中示范者持有隐藏信息造成的混杂问题，用混杂 MDP 形式化，引入反事实转移以区分数据可识别与不可识别的关联，并据此提出 CauCRL：从正负示范学习悲观反事实转移，在反事实 rollout 上训练 critic，在混杂任务上提升成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线无直接关联，但因果可识别性、正负示范对比与反事实 rollout 可能为 latent 轨迹训练、负例监督以及「latent 内容是否被因果使用」的评估提供概念线索，需人工核查其可迁移性。
